newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle sales thin at $64, growing - private.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle sales thin at $64, growing - private.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales were light early in Kansas at $64.00 per cwt, steady with thin trade on Monday, but activity was growing, feedlot sources said.
"There's some cattle trading at $64.00, and it looks like its going to be the market this week," a Kansas source said.

No volume estimates were available, but trading had just started and momentum was building, he said. No sales were reported early in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area yet, but they were seen soon at $64.00, several sources there said.

There still were owners holding out for at least $65.00, but resistance was crumbling amid knowledge that greater supplies of cattle are expected to be market-ready in the next six weeks, another Kansas feedlot operator said.
"I'm going to sell them at $64.00 because I know the next string will go at $63.00," he said.
Cattle owners were losing a "hefty chunk" of money at $64.00, with break-evens for those cattle selling this week at $67.00 to $68.00, the manager said.
"Most folks will want to hold out for another day, but the market has definitely established itself at $64.00," he said.
